name: js
description:
Control native apps and browser tabs on the user's computer by reading or operating their UI, in the background: apps are not raised or focused, and browser work happens in a tab group of its own. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. The tool result includes the documentation and, for an app or a tab, its initial UI state. Read it before continuing, and use only the APIs it describes.

When you need an inventory of apps, browsers and this session's tabs:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

If the user names an app, get it by name, bundle ID or path (a missing app is launched in the background):

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To open a URL in one of the user's browsers (the Chromium browsers running the nanocode extension; `"chrome"` is the connected Chrome or the only one, `"brave"` or `"edge"` by name, or an id from `cua.getState()`), in a background tab group; pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) when starting a task:

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("chrome", url, { sessionName });
```

To select a browser without opening a tab (its documentation covers `browser.tabs`, `browser.user.openTabs()` and `claimTab()` for the user's own tabs, `history`, and each tab's Playwright API `tab.playwright`):

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser();
```

A tab this session opened earlier, or a user tab by id or URL:

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabIdOrUrl, { browser: browserId });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what the code does.

name: js_add_node_module_dir
description: Add an absolute `node_modules` directory for package imports. The directory remains available after `js_reset`.

path.description: Absolute path to a node_modules directory to add to Node package resolution.

name: js_reset
description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call starts a fresh session. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state.

name: turn_ended
description: Notify cua_repl that a turn ended, so the browser tabs the turn used are closed. Repeated notifications for the same session and turn are ignored.
